thesis: Broadwind is a micro-cap diversified precision manufacturer levered to U.S. power-generation infrastructure, particularly the combined-cycle natural gas turbine supply chain (Industrial Solutions) and wind/heavy industrial fabrications. Q1 2026 orders grew 23% YoY with Gearing up 66% and Industrial Solutions up 44%, while FY2025 returned to GAAP profitability and record Industrial Solutions backlog. The asymmetric bull case rests on sustained gas-turbine/AI-power demand, margin operating leverage, and a low valuation versus the ~$6 analyst consensus target; risks are customer concentration, thin margins, cyclical wind exposure, and leverage.

financials.cash: ~$25M cash and availability under credit facility
financials.backlog: $38.1M (Industrial Solutions record at end of FY2025)

drivers: Industrial Solutions and Gearing orders sustain 20%+ YoY growth on gas-turbine and industrial replacement cycles
Heavy Fabrications stabilizes, removing a drag on consolidated revenue and sentiment
EBITDA margins expand toward 7–8% as revenue scales toward the $150M+ guided range
Debt paydown continues and micro-cap re-rates toward the upper end of sell-side targets

base_case.assumptions: Revenue lands in the guided $140–150M range, Adjusted EBITDA holds around $8–10M, and the company stays mildly profitable. The $6.00 analyst consensus acts as the anchor as H2 2026 orders convert.

risks: Wind capex collapses further and Heavy Fabrications orders continue to decline
Steel/input costs spike and fixed-price contracts compress margins
A key gas-turbine OEM customer pushes out orders, hurting Industrial Solutions backlog
EBITDA contracts toward breakeven, net debt/EBITDA rises above 3x, and an equity raise is required

catalysts.event: Report Q2 revenue (~$36.3M est.), Adjusted EBITDA margin, total orders, and any FY2026 guidance update or debt-paydown commentary
Conversion of Q1 order momentum into shipments and revenue; potential FY2026 guidance raise if Industrial Solutions backlog remains strong

key_risks: Customer concentration / OEM exposure in Industrial Solutions
Commodity and steel cost volatility pressuring fixed-price contract margins
Cyclical wind capex and production tax credit (PTC) uncertainty in Heavy Fabrications
Thin margins and small scale leave little room for execution error
Leverage and liquidity constraints if EBITDA contracts
Micro-cap liquidity and volatility amplifying price swings
